questions.q: In which year was Ujala Yojana launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2015.

Key Points

• Ujala Yojana was launched by the Government of India in 2015.

• The scheme is aimed at promoting energy efficiency by distributing LED bulbs to households at a subsidized rate.

• It was initially launched under the name "Domestic Efficient Lighting Programme (DELP)" and later renamed as Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All (UJALA).

• The scheme is implemented by Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL), a joint venture of PSUs under the Ministry of Power.

Additional Information

• Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL)

• EESL is a public sector entity responsible for implementing energy efficiency projects in India.

• It was established under the Ministry of Power, Government of India.

• EESL works towards promoting energy conservation and implementing energy efficiency projects on a large scale.

• It plays a critical role in implementing the Ujala Yojana by procuring and distributing LED bulbs.

• LED Bulbs

• Light Emitting Diode (LED) bulbs are highly energy-efficient lighting solutions.

• They consume significantly less electricity compared to traditional incandescent and CFL bulbs.

• LED bulbs have a longer lifespan and provide better illumination.

• They are environmentally friendly and help reduce carbon emissions.

• Energy Efficiency

• Energy efficiency refers to the optimal use of energy to perform a task, reducing energy consumption without compromising on output.

• It involves adopting practices and technologies that consume less energy for the same level of service or output.

• Energy efficiency measures help in reducing energy bills, conserving natural resources, and mitigating climate change.

• It is a key component of sustainable development and energy policy.

questions.q: Which of the following schemes of the Government of India is a part of the 'Target Group' approach?
options: Command Area Development & Water Management Programme (CADP)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Marginal Farmers Development Agency (MFDA).

Key Points

• The Marginal Farmers Development Agency (MFDA) was initiated by the Government of India to address the specific needs of marginal farmers.

• It aims to improve the socio-economic conditions of marginal farmers by providing them with necessary resources, training, and support.

• MFDA focuses on increasing agricultural productivity and income through various development programs and strategies tailored for the target group.

• The scheme includes components such as credit facilities, supply of inputs, irrigation, training, and market linkages to ensure comprehensive support for marginal farmers.

Additional Information

• Drought Prone Areas Programme (DPAP)

• DPAP is one of the earliest area development programs initiated by the Government of India to tackle the problems of drought in vulnerable areas.

• The primary objective is to minimize the adverse effects of drought on crop production, livestock, and productivity of land, water, and human resources.

• Hill Areas Development Programme (HADP)

• HADP was launched to ensure the socio-economic development of hill areas and their people.

• The program aims at addressing the unique problems faced by hill areas, including environmental degradation and lack of basic infrastructure.

• Command Area Development & Water Management Programme (CADP)

• CADP was initiated to enhance the utilization of irrigation potential created under major and medium irrigation projects.

• The program focuses on improving water use efficiency and ensuring equitable distribution of water.

questions.q: How many athletes were selected to represent India at the 1924 Paris Summer Olympics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 8.

Key Points

• India sent a team of 8 athletes to represent the country at the 1924 Paris Summer Olympics.

• This was the second time India participated in the Summer Olympics, the first being in 1900.

• The athletes competed in various track and field events.

• Although the Indian athletes did not win any medals at the 1924 Olympics, their participation marked an important step in India's Olympic history.

Additional Information

• 1924 Paris Summer Olympics

• The 1924 Summer Olympics, officially known as the Games of the VIII Olympiad, were held in Paris, France.

• This edition of the Olympic Games saw the participation of 3,089 athletes from 44 countries.

• These Games were notable for the introduction of the Olympic motto "Citius, Altius, Fortius" (Faster, Higher, Stronger).

• The 1924 Olympics also featured the first Olympic Village, where athletes could stay during the competitions.

• India's Participation in the Olympics

• India first participated in the Olympics in 1900, when Norman Pritchard represented the country and won two silver medals in athletics.

• After the 1924 Paris Olympics, India has consistently participated in every Summer Olympic Games.

• India's first gold medal was won by the men's field hockey team in the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics.

• Over the years, India has earned numerous medals in various sports, with significant achievements in field hockey, wrestling, shooting, and boxing.

• Track and Field Events

• Track and field is a sport comprising various competitive athletic contests based on running, jumping, and throwing.

• The sport is categorized under the umbrella of athletics, which also includes road running, cross country running, and racewalking.

• Track and field events are typically held on a running track and a grass field within a stadium.

• Some of the standard events in track and field include sprints, middle-distance and long-distance races, hurdles, relays, long jump, high jump, pole vault, shot put, discus throw, javelin throw, and hammer throw.

questions.q: For which of the following tribal music and dance forms was Arjun Singh Dhurve conferred with Tulsi Samman?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Baiga.

Key Points

• Arjun Singh Dhurve was honored with the Tulsi Samman for his exceptional contribution to the Baiga tribal music and dance form.

• The Baiga tribe is one of the prominent tribes in Madhya Pradesh, India, known for its vibrant culture and traditional practices.

• The Baiga dance is an integral part of their customs, often performed during festivals and important community events.

• The Tulsi Samman is a prestigious award given by the Madhya Pradesh government to individuals who have made significant contributions in the field of tribal art and culture.

Additional Information

• Tribal Music and Dance Forms

• Mardana: This is a traditional form of music and dance practiced by the tribal communities in various regions of India. It involves the use of traditional instruments and vibrant costumes.

• Pawara: A tribal dance form from the Pawara community, known for its rhythmic movements and cultural significance. It is usually performed during festivals and special occasions.

• Baiga: The Baiga tribe's dance form, which Arjun Singh Dhurve is recognized for, is characterized by its unique steps, rhythmic beats, and cultural expressions. The dancers often wear traditional attire made from natural materials.

• Jhumta: A traditional dance form performed by various tribal communities, often during harvest seasons and festivals. It involves group formations and synchronized movements.

• Tulsi Samman

• The Tulsi Samman is an award given by the Madhya Pradesh government to recognize and honor individuals who have made outstanding contributions to tribal art and culture.

• It aims to preserve and promote the rich cultural heritage of the tribal communities in the region.

• The award is named after the renowned poet and saint, Tulsidas, and is a symbol of cultural pride and recognition.

questions.q: In November 2021, the government declared November 15 as ‘Janjatiya Gaurav Divas’. It happens to be the birth anniversary of which of the following freedom fighters?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Birsa Munda.

Key Points

• Birsa Munda was an Indian tribal freedom fighter, religious leader, and folk hero who belonged to the Munda tribe.

• He spearheaded a tribal religious movement and is known for leading the Munda Rebellion against British colonial rule.

• His birth anniversary is on November 15, which is now celebrated as 'Janjatiya Gaurav Divas'.

• Birsa Munda's leadership and efforts in the fight against British oppression made him a significant figure in Indian history.

Additional Information

• Birsa Munda

• Born on November 15, 1875, in Ulihatu, Jharkhand, he played a key role in the Indian independence movement.

• He is known for his role in the Munda Rebellion (Ulgulan) against the British Raj and the landlords.

• Birsa Munda aimed to establish the Munda Raj and remove the British government and missionaries from the region.

• Despite his early death at the age of 25 on June 9, 1900, his legacy as a symbol of tribal resistance continues to inspire many.

• Janjatiya Gaurav Divas

• Janjatiya Gaurav Divas is a day to honor the contributions of tribal communities to the history and culture of India.

• The government of India declared November 15 as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas in 2021 to commemorate Birsa Munda's birth anniversary.

• This day is celebrated with various events and programs to recognize the sacrifices and achievements of tribal leaders and communities.

• It aims to promote tribal culture, heritage, and rights, ensuring the preservation and promotion of their unique identity.

• Munda Rebellion (Ulgulan)

• The Munda Rebellion, also known as Ulgulan, was a significant uprising against British colonial rule in the late 19th century.

• Led by Birsa Munda, the rebellion was a reaction to the exploitative policies of the British and local landlords.

• It sought to establish self-rule and end the oppression faced by the tribal communities.

• The rebellion, though eventually suppressed, highlighted the resilience and determination of the tribal people in their fight for justice.

questions.q: Hola Mohalla is a festival associated with which religion/belief?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sikhism.

Key Points

• Hola Mohalla is a significant festival celebrated by the Sikh community.

• The festival was started by the tenth Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, in 1701.

• Hola Mohalla is typically celebrated a day after the Hindu festival of Holi.

• It is a week-long festival that involves mock battles, exhibitions, martial arts, poetry, and music.

Additional Information

• Sikhism

• Sikhism is a monotheistic religion that originated in the Punjab region of the Indian subcontinent around the end of the 15th century.

• The fundamental beliefs of Sikhism, articulated in the sacred scripture Guru Granth Sahib, include faith and meditation on the name of the one creator, unity of all humankind, engaging in selfless service, striving for justice for the benefit and prosperity of all, and honest conduct and livelihood while living a householder's life.

• The Sikh community celebrates various festivals like Baisakhi, Guru Nanak Jayanti, and Hola Mohalla.

• Sikhism was founded by Guru Nanak and has ten gurus, with Guru Gobind Singh being the last human Guru. Guru Granth Sahib is the eternal Guru of the Sikhs.

• Guru Gobind Singh

• Guru Gobind Singh was the tenth Sikh Guru, a spiritual master, warrior, poet, and philosopher.

• He was born on 22 December 1666 in Patna, Bihar, India.

• He founded the Khalsa in 1699, a collective body of initiated Sikhs, and introduced the Five Ks, five articles of faith that Khalsa Sikhs wear at all times.

• Guru Gobind Singh also declared that the Guru Granth Sahib, the Sikh holy scripture, would be the eternal Guru after him.

• Holi

• Holi is a popular ancient Hindu festival, also known as the "festival of colors" or the "festival of love".

• The festival signifies the arrival of spring, the end of winter, the blossoming of love, and for many, it is a festive day to meet others, play and laugh, forget and forgive, and repair broken relationships.

• The festival is also celebrated as a thanksgiving for a good harvest.

• It lasts for a night and a day, starting on the evening of the Purnima (Full Moon day) falling in the Hindu calendar month of Phalguna, which falls around the middle of March in the Gregorian calendar.

questions.q: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts led to formation of the Goods and Services Tax Council?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 101st Constitutional Amendment Act.

Key Points

• The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act was passed by the Indian Parliament in August 2016.

• This amendment led to the introduction of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India, which came into effect on 1st July 2017.

• The GST Council was formed as per Article 279A of the Indian Constitution, inserted by the 101st Amendment.

• The GST Council is responsible for making recommendations on the rates of taxes, goods and services that may be subjected or exempted from GST, and other related matters.

Additional Information

• 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act

• This amendment came into effect in 2018.

• It granted constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC).

• Article 338B was inserted to provide for the NCBC.

• 100th Constitutional Amendment Act

• This amendment was passed in 2015.

• It dealt with the exchange of certain enclaves between India and Bangladesh and the demarcation of the boundary between the two countries.

• It facilitated the implementation of the Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) between India and Bangladesh.

• 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act

• This amendment came into effect in 2019.

• It introduced a 10% reservation for economically weaker sections (EWS) in government jobs and educational institutions.

• Articles 15(6) and 16(6) were added to the Constitution to enable this reservation.

• Goods and Services Tax (GST)

• GST is a comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based tax that is levied on every value addition.

• It replaced multiple indirect taxes previously levied by the central and state governments.

• GST is categorized into Central GST (CGST), State GST (SGST), Integrated GST (IGST), and Union Territory GST (UTGST).

• The GST Council, chaired by the Union Finance Minister, is a federal body where both the center and the states participate in the decision-making process.

questions.q: Which coal is low-grade, brown and soft with high moisture content?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lignite.

Key Points

• Lignite is a type of coal that is considered to be low-grade due to its relatively low energy content.

• It is brown in color and has a soft texture, making it easier to break apart compared to harder forms of coal.

• Lignite has a high moisture content, sometimes as much as 45-66%, which reduces its efficiency as a fuel source.

• Despite its lower quality, lignite is often used in electricity generation, particularly in power plants located near lignite mines.

Additional Information

• Metallurgical Coal

• Also known as coking coal, it is primarily used in steel production.

• It has a high carbon content and low impurities, which are essential for producing high-quality coke.

• Metallurgical coal undergoes a coking process where it is heated in the absence of air to remove volatile substances, leaving behind a solid carbon mass called coke.

• Bituminous Coal

• It is a middle-rank coal between sub-bituminous and anthracite.

• Bituminous coal is used extensively for electricity generation and as a fuel in industries.

• It has a higher carbon content than lignite and sub-bituminous coal, providing more energy when burned.

• Anthracite

• It is the highest rank of coal due to its high carbon content and low impurities.

• Anthracite is hard, shiny, and has the highest energy content of all coal types.

• It is used for heating residential and commercial buildings and in some industrial processes.

questions.q: Which of the following gases plays an important role in welding titanium, aluminium, stainless steel, and magnesium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Argon.

Key Points

• Argon is an inert gas, which means it does not react with the materials being welded, making it ideal for welding processes.

• It is used as a shielding gas to protect the weld area from atmospheric gases such as oxygen, nitrogen, and water vapor that can cause defects in the weld.

• Argon provides a stable arc and excellent control over the welding process, which is crucial for welding materials like titanium, aluminium, stainless steel, and magnesium.

• It is often used in Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW) and Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW) processes.

Additional Information

• Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW)

• Also known as Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) welding, GTAW uses a non-consumable tungsten electrode to produce the weld.

• Argon is the most commonly used shielding gas in GTAW due to its inert properties and ability to create a stable arc.

• GTAW is known for producing high-quality, precision welds and is often used for welding thin materials.

• Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW)

• Also known as Metal Inert Gas (MIG) welding, GMAW uses a continuous wire feed as an electrode and an inert or semi-inert gas mixture for shielding.

• Argon is often used in GMAW, sometimes mixed with other gases like carbon dioxide or helium to optimize the welding process for different materials.

• GMAW is widely used in industrial applications due to its high welding speed and ease of automation.

• Importance of Shielding Gas

• Shielding gases like argon protect the weld pool from contamination by atmospheric gases, which can cause porosity and weld defects.

• They help stabilize the arc, improve weld quality, and ensure a clean and strong weld.

• The choice of shielding gas depends on the materials being welded and the specific welding process used.

• It is given to the exponents of Hindustani classical music in recognition of their contribution and excellence in the field.

• The award is named after the legendary musician Tansen, who was one of the nine gems in the court of Emperor Akbar.

• The Tansen Samman includes a cash prize and a citation, honoring the recipient's lifelong dedication to Indian classical music.

Additional Information

• Hindustani Classical Music

• Hindustani classical music is one of the two major traditions of Indian classical music, the other being Carnatic music.

• It originated in North India and has a rich history that dates back to the Vedic times.

• The music is characterized by its raga (melodic framework) and tala (rhythmic cycle).

• Some of the prominent exponents of Hindustani classical music include Ravi Shankar, Zakir Hussain, and Bhimsen Joshi.

• Tansen

• Tansen was a prominent figure in Indian classical music and is often regarded as one of the greatest musicians of all time.

• He was a musician in the court of Emperor Akbar in the 16th century.

• Tansen is known for his contributions to the development of Hindustani classical music, especially the dhrupad style of singing.

questions.q: The term Blue Line is associated with which of the following games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ice Hockey.

Key Points

• The term "Blue Line" is a significant part of the game Ice Hockey.

• It refers to the lines that divide the hockey rink into three zones: the defending zone, neutral zone, and attacking zone.

• The blue lines play a crucial role in determining offside violations in the game of ice hockey.

• They are essential in regulating the flow of the game and ensuring that players adhere to the rules related to positioning on the rink.

Additional Information

• Offside Rule in Ice Hockey

• The offside rule is one of the fundamental rules in ice hockey, aimed at preventing players from gaining an unfair advantage.

• A player is considered offside if they enter the attacking zone before the puck crosses the blue line.

• If an offside violation occurs, the referee stops the play, and a faceoff is conducted in the neutral zone to resume the game.

• Understanding the offside rule is crucial for players and coaches as it impacts offensive strategies and game planning.

• Zones on the Rink

• The ice hockey rink is divided into three zones by two blue lines: the defending zone, the neutral zone, and the attacking zone.

• The defending zone is the area between the blue line closest to a team's goal and the end boards.

• The neutral zone lies between the two blue lines, where much of the game's transition play occurs.

• The attacking zone is the area between the blue line farthest from a team's goal and the end boards, where a team aims to score goals.

• Importance of the Blue Line

• The blue lines are critical for maintaining the structure and flow of the game, ensuring that players adhere to the rules of positioning.

• They are used to judge offside violations and play a role in determining where faceoffs occur on the rink.

• Blue lines also contribute to the strategic aspects of the game, influencing how teams execute their offensive and defensive plays.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding circular flow of income?
options: Savings as well as government expenditure are injections to the circular flow.
The income of one sector becomes the expenditure of the other.
In a circular flow, leakages are equal to injections.
The real flow and monetary flow move in a circular manner in an opposite direction.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Savings as well as government expenditure are injections to the circular flow..

Key Points

• Savings are considered a leakage from the circular flow of income as they represent income not spent on consumption.

• Government expenditure is an injection into the circular flow as it represents spending that adds to the overall demand in the economy.

• In a closed economy with no government intervention, savings would be equal to investment.

• The correct representation would be that investment and government spending are injections, while savings, taxes, and imports are leakages.

Additional Information

• Circular Flow of Income

• The circular flow of income is a model that depicts how money flows through the economy between households and firms.

• In this model, households provide factors of production (labor, land, capital) to firms, and in return, they receive income (wages, rent, interest, profit).

• Households then use this income to purchase goods and services from firms, completing the cycle.

• Leakages and Injections

• Leakages are non-consumption uses of income, including savings, taxes, and imports. They represent money that leaves the circular flow.

• Injections are additions to the income of firms, including investment, government spending, and exports. They represent money entering the circular flow.

• In a balanced circular flow, the total value of leakages is equal to the total value of injections.

• Real Flow and Monetary Flow

• The real flow refers to the flow of physical goods and services and the factors of production.

• The monetary flow refers to the flow of money in the form of income and expenditure.

• In the circular flow model, the real flow and monetary flow move in opposite directions to each other.

questions.q: The type of reaction that is typically found when a material that is required for the reaction to proceed, such as a surface or a catalyst, is saturated by the reactants is called a  order reaction.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is zero order reaction.

Key Points

• In a zero-order reaction, the rate of reaction is independent of the concentration of the reactants.

• These reactions are commonly seen in catalytic processes where the catalyst surface is saturated by the reactants.

• In such reactions, the rate of reaction remains constant until the reactant concentration is significantly depleted.

• Zero-order kinetics is often observed in heterogeneous catalysis and other situations where a limiting step is saturated.

Additional Information

• First-order Reaction

• A first-order reaction is one where the rate is directly proportional to the concentration of one reactant.

• The rate law for a first-order reaction can be expressed as: Rate = k[A], where k is the rate constant and [A] is the concentration of the reactant.

• These reactions often involve unimolecular processes.

• Examples include radioactive decay and certain substitution reactions in organic chemistry.

• Second-order Reaction

• A second-order reaction's rate is proportional to the square of the concentration of one reactant or the product of the concentrations of two reactants.

• The rate law can be written as: Rate = k[A]² or Rate = k[A][B], depending on the reaction mechanism.

• These reactions often involve bimolecular processes.

• Examples include the reaction between hydrogen and iodine to form hydrogen iodide.

• Third-order Reaction

• A third-order reaction's rate depends on the concentration of three reactants or the concentration of one reactant raised to the third power, or other combinations summing to three.

• The rate law can be expressed as: Rate = k[A]³ or other combinations.

• These reactions are less common compared to first and second-order reactions.

• An example is the reaction between nitric oxide and oxygen to form nitrogen dioxide.

questions.q: The ratio of circumference and diameter of a circle is 22 : 7. If the circumference is 33 cm, then the radius of the circle is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given the ratio of Circumference to Diameter = 22 : 7

Here, 22 units of Circumference → 33 cm

1 unit → 33 ÷ 22 = 1.5 cm

Diameter (7 units) = 7 × 1.5 = 10.5 cm

Radius = Diameter ÷ 2 = 10.5 ÷ 2 = 5.25 cm

∴ The correct answer is 5.25 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Circumference of the circle (C) = 33 cm

Ratio of Circumference (C) to Diameter (D) = 22 : 7



Formula Used:

Diameter (D) = Circumference × (7 ÷ 22)

Radius (r) = Diameter ÷ 2

Calculations:

⇒ C ÷ D = 22 ÷ 7

⇒ 33 ÷ D = 22 ÷ 7

⇒ D = (33 × 7) ÷ 22

⇒ D = (3 × 7) ÷ 2

⇒ D = 21 ÷ 2 = 10.5 cm

⇒ Radius (r) = 10.5 ÷ 2 = 5.25 cm

∴ The correct answer is 5.25 cm.

Additional Information

Circumference of a Circle

The total boundary length is given by C = 2πr or C = πD, where π ≈ 22 ÷ 7.

Area of a Circle

The total space enclosed within the boundary is evaluated as Area = πr².

Semicircle Properties

The perimeter of a semicircle includes both the curved path and the straight diameter: P = πr + 2r. Its Area is πr² ÷ 2.

questions.q: The monthly income of Ramesh in year 2021 was ₹18,600 and his monthly expenditure was ₹12,400. In year 2022 his income increased by 15% and his expenditure increased by 8%. Find the percentage increase in his savings.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Initial Income : Expenditure : Savings = 18600 : 12400 : 6200 = 3 : 2 : 1.

We know, Income = Expenditure + Savings ⇒ 3 = 2 + 1.

Applying the net percentage change equation (Weighted Average):

⇒ 3 × 15% = (2 × 8%) + (1 × x%)

⇒ 45% = 16% + x% ⇒ x = 29%

∴ The correct answer is 29%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Income = ₹18,600

Initial Expenditure = ₹12,400

Formula Used:

Savings = Income − Expenditure

Percentage Increase = (Increase ÷ Original Value) × 100



Calculations:

⇒ Initial Savings = ₹18,600 − ₹12,400 = ₹6,200

⇒ New Income = ₹18,600 × (100 + 15)% = ₹18,600 × 1.15 = ₹21,390

⇒ New Expenditure = ₹12,400 × (100 + 8)% = ₹12,400 × 1.08 = ₹13,392

⇒ New Savings = ₹21,390 − ₹13,392 = ₹7,998

⇒ Increase in Savings = ₹7,998 − ₹6,200 = ₹1,798

⇒ Percentage increase in Savings = (1,798 ÷ 6,200) × 100 = 29%

∴ The correct answer is 29%.

Additional Information

Income, Expenditure & Savings Relation

Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any percentage change in income is strictly distributed between expenditure and savings based on their proportional weightage.

Weighted Average Method

When a quantity is divided into two parts in the ratio a : b, and the parts change by x% and y%, the net percentage change is given by (ax + by) ÷ (a + b).

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100.

questions.q: A class of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 60, and that of the rest is 80. What is the average score of the class?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the base average be 60 (average of 12 students).

The other 18 students have an average of 80, which is +20 more than the base.

Total excess score brought by these 18 students = 18 × 20 = +360.

Distribute this excess equally among all 30 students = 360 ÷ 30 = +12.

Overall Average = Base Average + Distributed Excess = 60 + 12 = 72.

∴ The correct answer is 72 marks.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total students in the class = 30

Average score of 12 students = 60

Number of remaining students = 30 − 12 = 18

Average score of the 18 students = 80

Formula Used:

Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The given expression follows the multiple-angle trigonometric identity directly.

Identity: sin(3θ) = 3sin(θ) − 4sin³(θ)

Here, the angle is θ = 15°.

Expression = 3sin(15°) − 4sin³(15°) = sin(3 × 15°)

⇒ sin(45°) = 1/√2

∴ The correct answer is 1/√2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression: 3sin 15° − 4sin³ 15°

Formula Used:

Standard exact value: sin 15° = (√3 − 1) / 2√2

Algebraic identity: (a − b)³ = a³ − 3a²b + 3ab² − b³

Calculations:

⇒ 3sin 15° = 3 × [(√3 − 1) / 2√2] = (3√3 − 3) / 2√2

⇒ sin³ 15° = [(√3 − 1) / 2√2]³

⇒ Expand Numerator: (√3 − 1)³ = (√3)³ − 3(√3)²(1) + 3(√3)(1)² − (1)³

⇒ (√3 − 1)³ = 3√3 − 9 + 3√3 − 1 = 6√3 − 10

⇒ Cube Denominator: (2√2)³ = 16√2

⇒ 4sin³ 15° = 4 × [(6√3 − 10) / 16√2] = (6√3 − 10) / 4√2

⇒ Now substitute the expanded parts into the original expression:

⇒ Expression = [(3√3 − 3) / 2√2] − [(6√3 − 10) / 4√2]

⇒ Make denominators equal by multiplying the first term by 2/2:

⇒ Expression = [(6√3 − 6) / 4√2] − [(6√3 − 10) / 4√2]

⇒ Combine terms: [6√3 − 6 − 6√3 + 10] / 4√2

⇒ Expression = 4 / 4√2 = 1/√2

∴ The correct answer is 1/√2.

Additional Information

Multiple Angle Identity for Cosine

Similar to the sine function, the cosine triple angle formula is given by: cos(3θ) = 4cos³(θ) − 3cos(θ).

Double Angle Identities

Important double angle formulas include: sin(2θ) = 2sin(θ)cos(θ) and cos(2θ) = cos²(θ) − sin²(θ) = 1 − 2sin²(θ).

Standard Trigonometric Values for 15°

For competitive exams, it is highly useful to memorize these common exact values: sin(15°) = (√3 − 1) / 2√2 and cos(15°) = (√3 + 1) / 2√2.

Shortcut Trick

Given, Gain = 1/5 of Selling Price (SP).

Let SP = 5 units. Then, Gain = 1 unit.

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Gain = 5 − 1 = 4 units.

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%.

*Note: The actual SP value (₹40620) is not needed for calculating the percentage.*

∴ The correct answer is 25%.

CP = SP − Gain

⇒ Gain = (1 ÷ 5) × 40620 = ₹8124

⇒ CP = 40620 − 8124 = ₹32496

⇒ Gain % = (8124 ÷ 32496) × 100

⇒ Gain % = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%

∴ The correct answer is 25%.

Additional Information

Base of Calculation

Profit and loss percentages are always calculated on the true Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise in the question.

Standard Profit Formula

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100, where Profit = SP − CP.

Profit on Selling Price

When profit is calculated based on SP instead of CP, the actual Cost Price is smaller than SP, making the actual real profit percentage (on CP) higher than the given profit percentage on SP.

questions.q: The single discount equivalent to the discount series of 15%, 20% and 5% is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using the effective discount formula: Equivalent Discount = a + b − (a×b)/100

Equivalent discount of 15% and 20% = 15 + 20 − (15×20)/100 = 35 − 3 = 32%

Equivalent discount of 32% and 5% = 32 + 5 − (32×5)/100 = 37 − 1.6 = 35.4%

∴ The correct answer is 35.4%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Successive discount series = 15%, 20%, 5%

Formula Used:

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − D₁)/100 × (100 − D₂)/100 × (100 − D₃)/100



Calculations:

⇒ Let the Marked Price (MP) be 100.

⇒ Price after 1st discount of 15% = 100 × (100 − 15)/100 = 85

⇒ Price after 2nd discount of 20% = 85 × (100 − 20)/100 = 85 × 80/100 = 68

⇒ Final Selling Price after 3rd discount of 5% = 68 × (100 − 5)/100 = 68 × 95/100 = 64.6

⇒ Single Equivalent Discount = MP − Final SP

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 100 − 64.6 = 35.4%

∴ The correct answer is 35.4%.

Additional Information

Successive Discount Formula

For two consecutive discounts a% and b%, the single equivalent discount is [a + b − (a×b)/100]%.

Marked Price (MP) & Cost Price (CP) Relation

The direct relationship is given by: CP/MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).

Successive Percentage Multiplier

For a series of discounts D₁, D₂, D₃, the final value = Initial Base × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100) × (1 − D₃/100).

questions.q: A tap can fill a cistern in 10 minutes and another tap can empty it in 12 minutes. If both the taps are open, the time (in hours) taken to fill the tank will be:

Here, x = 10 mins and y = 12 mins.

Time = (10 × 12) ÷ (12 − 10) = 120 ÷ 2 = 60 minutes.

Converting into hours: 60 minutes = 1 hour.

∴ The correct answer is 1 hour.

questions.q: Cindy bought 15 apples and 12 oranges and paid a sum of ₹447 for the purchase. Which of the statements given below is inconsistent with the information given in the previous statement, leading to no possible prices of the two fruits?
options: Purchased 25 apples and 20 oranges and paid a sum of ₹745
Purchased 10 apples and 13 oranges and paid a sum of ₹353
Purchased 12 apples and 8 oranges and paid a sum of ₹340
Purchased 35 apples and 28 oranges and paid a sum of ₹1,029
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given the cost of 15 apples and 12 oranges is ₹447, we divide by 3 to get the cost of 5 apples and 4 oranges as ₹149.

An inconsistent statement will have the same ratio of apples to oranges (5:4) but an equivalent cost that does not match ₹149.

In the fourth statement, 35 apples and 28 oranges are in a 5:4 ratio.

However, dividing its cost ₹1,029 by 7 gives ₹147 for 5 apples and 4 oranges.

Since ₹147 ≠ ₹149, it contradicts the given data, leading to no possible solutions.

∴ The correct answer is Purchased 35 apples and 28 oranges and paid a sum of ₹1,029.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost of 15 apples and 12 oranges = ₹447

Formula Used:

For a system of linear equations a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂:

If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂, the system is inconsistent and yields no possible solution.

Calculation:

⇒ Let the price of 1 apple be a and 1 orange be o.

⇒ 15a + 12o = 447

⇒ Checking Statement 1: 25a + 20o = 745

⇒ 15/25 = 12/20 = 447/745 (ratio simplifies to 3/5 for all). Consistent (Infinite solutions).

⇒ Checking Statement 2: 10a + 13o = 353

⇒ 15/10 ≠ 12/13. Consistent (Unique solution).

⇒ Checking Statement 3: 12a + 8o = 340

⇒ 15/12 ≠ 12/8. Consistent (Unique solution).

⇒ Checking Statement 4: 35a + 28o = 1029

⇒ a₁/a₂ = 15/35 = 3/7

⇒ b₁/b₂ = 12/28 = 3/7

⇒ c₁/c₂ = 447/1029 = 149/343

⇒ Here, a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂

⇒ Because the ratios of coefficients are equal but differ from the constant ratio, the system is inconsistent.

∴ The correct answer is Purchased 35 apples and 28 oranges and paid a sum of ₹1,029.

Additional Information

Unique Solution

A system of equations has a unique solution if the lines intersect at exactly one point. Condition: a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂.

No Solution (Inconsistent System)

A system has no solution if the lines are perfectly parallel and never intersect. Condition: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂.

Infinite Solutions (Dependent System)

A system has infinitely many solutions if the equations represent the exact same line. Condition: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.

questions.q: From a point T, a tangent TP at point P, is drawn to a circle with centre O. A secant TQR (point Q is near to point T) is drawn from the point T. ∆PQR is inscribed into the circle by joining the points P, Q and R. Draw lines OQ and OR. If ∠PTQ is 27° and ∠TPQ = 55°, what is the degree measure of ∠ROQ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles. For ΔTQP, the exterior angle at Q is ∠PQR.

∠PQR = ∠PTQ + ∠TPQ = 27° + 55° = 82°.

By the Alternate Segment Theorem, the angle between the tangent TP and chord PQ equals the angle in the alternate segment: ∠PRQ = ∠TPQ = 55°.

In ΔPQR, ∠QPR = 180° − (∠PQR + ∠PRQ) = 180° − (82° + 55°) = 43°.

The central angle ∠ROQ is twice the angle subtended at the circumference by the same arc: ∠ROQ = 2 × ∠QPR = 2 × 43° = 86°.

∴ The correct answer is 86°.

Alternate Method

Given:

T is a point outside a circle with center O.

TP is a tangent to the circle at point P.

TQR is a secant intersecting the circle at points Q and R (with Q nearer to T).

∠PTQ = 27° and ∠TPQ = 55°.

questions.q: If x² + 1 = x , then the value of x¹² + x⁶ + 1 is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If x² − x + 1 = 0, it is a standard algebraic result that x³ = −1.

We need to evaluate x¹² + x⁶ + 1.

Rewrite the expression in terms of x³: (x³)⁴ + (x³)² + 1.

Substitute x³ = −1: (−1)⁴ + (−1)² + 1.

⇒ 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Alternate Method

Given:

x² + 1 = x

Formula Used:

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)

Calculation:

⇒ x² − x + 1 = 0

Multiplying both sides by (x + 1):

⇒ (x + 1)(x² − x + 1) = 0 × (x + 1)

Using the identity for a³ + b³:

⇒ x³ + 1³ = 0

⇒ x³ = −1

Now, substitute x³ = −1 into the given expression: x¹² + x⁶ + 1

⇒ (x³)⁴ + (x³)² + 1

⇒ (−1)⁴ + (−1)² + 1

⇒ 1 + 1 + 1

⇒ 3

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Additional Information

Sum of Cubes Identity

The identity a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) is very useful for powers of complex roots. If x² − x + 1 = 0, then multiplying by (x + 1) gives x³ = −1.

Difference of Cubes Identity

The identity a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) is used similarly. If x² + x + 1 = 0, then multiplying by (x − 1) gives x³ = 1.

Complex Roots of Unity

The roots of x² + x + 1 = 0 are known as the non-real cube roots of unity (denoted as ω and ω²). They satisfy ω³ = 1 and 1 + ω + ω² = 0.

questions.q: A well with 14 cm radius is dug 23 cm deep. Find the volume of the earth taken out of it.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The well is dug in the shape of a cylinder.

Volume of earth dug out = Volume of the cylinder = πr²h

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 14 × 14 × 23

⇒ Volume = 22 × 2 × 14 × 23 = 14,168

∴ The correct answer is 14,168 cm³.

Alternate Method



Given:

Radius of the well (r) = 14 cm

Depth of the well (h) = 23 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of a cylinder = π × r² × h

Calculation:

⇒ Volume of earth taken out = (22/7) × (14)² × 23

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 196 × 23

⇒ Volume = 22 × 28 × 23

⇒ Volume = 616 × 23

⇒ Volume = 14,168 cm³

∴ The correct answer is 14,168 cm³.

Additional Information

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a Cylinder

The area of the outer curved surface is calculated using the formula: CSA = 2πrh.

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved surface plus the top and bottom circular bases: TSA = 2πr(r + h).

Volume of a Hollow Cylinder

If a cylinder is hollow with outer radius R and inner radius r, its material volume is given by: Volume = π(R² − r²)h.

Relation with a Cone

A cone having the exact same base radius and height as a cylinder will always have one-third of the cylinder's volume: V = (1/3)πr²h.

questions.q: Pranav borrows a sum of ₹335180 at the rate of 13% per annum simple interest. At the end of the first year, he repays ₹23060 towards return of principal amount borrowed. If Pranav clears all pending dues at the end of the second year, including interest payment that accrued during the first year, how much does he pay (in ₹) at the end of the second year?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total amount if no repayment is made = 335180 + (26% of 335180) = 335180 + 87146.8 = ₹422326.8

Since ₹23060 is paid towards the principal at the end of Year 1, interest is saved for Year 2 on this amount.

Total effective value of this repayment = Principal paid + Interest saved for 1 year = 23060 + (13% of 23060) = 23060 + 2997.8 = ₹26057.8

Remaining amount to pay at the end of 2nd year = Total Amount − Total effective repayment

⇒ Amount to pay = 422326.8 − 26057.8 = ₹396269

∴ The correct answer is ₹396269.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹335180

Rate (R) = 13% per annum

Repayment at the end of Year 1 = ₹23060 (towards principal)



Calculations:

⇒ Interest accrued during the 1st year (I₁) = (335180 × 13) ÷ 100 = ₹43573.4

⇒ Pranav repays ₹23060 towards the principal at the end of the 1st year.

⇒ Remaining principal for the 2nd year = 335180 − 23060 = ₹312120

⇒ Interest accrued during the 2nd year (I₂) = (312120 × 13) ÷ 100 = ₹40575.6

⇒ Total pending dues at the end of the 2nd year = Remaining Principal + 1st Year Interest + 2nd Year Interest

⇒ Total Amount = 312120 + 43573.4 + 40575.6 = ₹396269

∴ The correct answer is ₹396269.

Additional Information

Simple Interest (SI)

Calculated strictly on the principal amount over a period. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Partial Repayment Rule

When a borrower makes a partial payment, it typically covers the accrued interest first. However, if explicitly mentioned (as in this case), it is deducted directly from the principal, which sequentially lowers the interest for future periods.

SI vs CI Difference

In Simple Interest, unpaid accrued interest does not earn further interest. In Compound Interest, accrued interest is added to the principal (A = P(1 + R/100)T), creating an "interest on interest" effect.

questions.q: In the figure shown above, quadrilateral PQRS has its vertices on the circumference of the circle with centre O. If m∠QOS = 20x° and m∠QRS = 26x°, then what is the value of ‘x’?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is twice the angle subtended at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

⇒ m∠QPS = m∠QOS ÷ 2 = 20x° ÷ 2 = 10x°

In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary (sum to 180°).

⇒ m∠QPS + m∠QRS = 180°

⇒ 10x° + 26x° = 180° ⇒ 36x = 180 ⇒ x = 5

∴ The correct answer is 5.

Alternate Method

Given:

m∠QOS = 20x°

m∠QRS = 26x°

Formula Used:

1. Angle at the center = 2 × Angle at the circumference

2. Sum of opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral = 180°



Calculations:

By the angle at the center theorem, the angle subtended by the arc QS at the remaining part of the circle (at vertex P) is half the angle subtended at the center.

⇒ m∠QPS = m∠QOS ÷ 2

⇒ m∠QPS = 20x° ÷ 2 = 10x°

Since all the vertices P, Q, R, and S lie exactly on the circumference of the circle, PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral.

In a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of any pair of opposite angles is equal to 180°.

⇒ m∠QPS + m∠QRS = 180°

Substitute the respective angle values:

⇒ 10x° + 26x° = 180°

⇒ 36x = 180

⇒ x = 180 ÷ 36

⇒ x = 5

∴ The correct answer is 5.

Additional Information

Cyclic Quadrilateral

A quadrilateral whose all four vertices lie on the circumference of a circle. The sum of either pair of opposite angles is always exactly 180°.

Angle at Center Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the center of the circle is double the angle subtended by the same arc at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same arc at any point on the circumference of the circle are always equal to each other.

questions.q: Seema walks around a circular field at the rate of 3 rounds per hour, while Priya runs around it at the rate of 8 rounds per hour. They start in the same direction from the same point at 11:54 PM. They shall first cross each other at:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Relative speed in the same direction = 8 − 3 = 5 rounds per hour.

This means Priya gains 5 complete rounds over Seema in 60 minutes.

They will cross each other when Priya gains exactly 1 complete round.

Time to gain 1 round = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 minutes.

Crossing time = 11:54 p.m. + 12 minutes = 12:06 a.m.

∴ The correct answer is 12:06 a.m.

Alternate Method



Given:

⇒ Speed of Seema = 3 rounds/hr

⇒ Speed of Priya = 8 rounds/hr

⇒ Starting time = 11:54 p.m.

Formula Used:

⇒ Relative Speed (same direction) = Speed₁ − Speed₂

⇒ Time to cross for the first time = 1 round distance ÷ Relative Speed

Calculations:

⇒ Since they are moving in the same direction, relative speed = 8 − 3 = 5 rounds/hr

⇒ They cross each other when the faster person (Priya) covers exactly 1 more round than the slower person (Seema).

⇒ Time taken to gain 1 round = 1 ÷ 5 hours

⇒ Time taken in minutes = (1/5) × 60 = 12 minutes

⇒ Crossing time = 11:54 p.m. + 12 minutes

⇒ 11:54 p.m. + 6 minutes = 12:00 a.m. (Midnight)

⇒ 12:00 a.m. + 6 minutes = 12:06 a.m.

∴ The correct answer is 12:06 a.m.

Additional Information

Circular Motion (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction on a circular track, the time taken to meet for the first time anywhere on the track is calculated as Track Length ÷ (Speed₁ − Speed₂).

Circular Motion (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed increases. The time taken to meet for the first time is Track Length ÷ (Speed₁ + Speed₂).

Meeting at the Starting Point

The time taken for both runners to meet exactly at the starting point is the LCM (Least Common Multiple) of the individual times taken by each to complete one full round.

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

If the ratio of their speeds is a:b (in simplest form), they will meet at exactly (a − b) distinct points if running in the same direction, and at (a + b) distinct points if running in opposite directions.

questions.q: 'x' varies directly with the cube of 'y', and inversely with the square of 'z'. If x = 361​ when y = 2 and z = 3, then what is the value of 800x when y = 3 and z = 5?
options: 8009​
9800​
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given x ∝ y³ / z², we can directly compare the two states using ratio method:

x₁ / x₂ = (y₁ / y₂)³ × (z₂ / z₁)²

(1/36) / x₂ = (2 / 3)³ × (5 / 3)² = (8 / 27) × (25 / 9) = 200 / 243

x₂ = (1/36) × (243 / 200) = 27 / 800

800x₂ = 800 × (27 / 800) = 27

∴ The correct answer is 27.

Alternate Method

Given:

x varies directly with the cube of y and inversely with the square of z.

⇒ x = k × (y³ / z²), where k is a constant.



Calculations:

Substitute the given values (x = 1/36, y = 2, z = 3) to find k:

⇒ 1/36 = k × (2³ / 3²)

⇒ 1/36 = k × (8 / 9)

⇒ k = (1/36) × (9 / 8) = 1 / 32

Now, substitute y = 3 and z = 5 to find the new value of x:

⇒ x = (1/32) × (3³ / 5²)

⇒ x = (1/32) × (27 / 25)

⇒ x = 27 / 800

Find the required value of 800x:

⇒ 800x = 800 × (27 / 800) = 27

∴ The correct answer is 27.

Additional Information

Direct Variation

If two quantities x and y vary directly, their ratio is constant: x / y = k or x = ky. As one increases, the other increases proportionally.

Inverse Variation

If x and y vary inversely, their product is constant: x × y = k or x = k / y. As one increases, the other decreases proportionally.

Joint Variation

When a quantity varies directly with one variable and inversely with another, the equations combine as shown in this problem: x = k × (y / z).

questions.q: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 6?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a number to be divisible by 6, it must be even (divisible by 2) and its digit sum must be divisible by 3.

Eliminate odd options immediately: 12581 and 62233 are rejected.

Check 128530: Sum = 1 + 2 + 8 + 5 + 3 + 0 = 19 (Not divisible by 3).

Check 438750: Sum = 4 + 3 + 8 + 7 + 5 + 0 = 27 (Divisible by 3). It satisfies both conditions.

∴ The correct answer is 438750.

Alternate Method

Given:

Numbers to check: 128530, 12581, 438750, and 62233

Concept Used:

Divisibility by 6: A number is divisible by 6 if and only if it is divisible by both 2 and 3.

Divisibility by 2: The unit digit must be an even number (0, 2, 4, 6, 8).

Divisibility by 3: The sum of the digits must be a multiple of 3.

Calculations:

⇒ Let us evaluate the given options one by one:

⇒ Option 1: 128530

⇒ Unit digit is 0, which is even (divisible by 2).

⇒ Sum of digits = 1 + 2 + 8 + 5 + 3 + 0 = 19

⇒ Since 19 is not divisible by 3, 128530 is not divisible by 6.

⇒ Option 2: 12581

⇒ Unit digit is 1, which is odd (not divisible by 2). So, it is not divisible by 6.

⇒ Option 3: 438750

⇒ Unit digit is 0, which is even (divisible by 2).

⇒ Sum of digits = 4 + 3 + 8 + 7 + 5 + 0 = 27

⇒ Since 27 is divisible by 3, and the number is even, 438750 is divisible by 6.

⇒ Option 4: 62233

⇒ Unit digit is 3, which is odd (not divisible by 2). So, it is not divisible by 6.

∴ The correct answer is 438750.

Additional Information

Divisibility Rule of 4

A number is divisible by 4 if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4.

Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 9.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.q: If secθ + tanθ = x, then find sinθ.
options: 1−x2x2+1​
1+2x2x2−1​
1+x2x2−1​
1+x21−x2​
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Put θ = 30° in the given equation.

⇒ x = sec 30° + tan 30° = 2/√3 + 1/√3 = 3/√3 = √3

We need to find sin 30°, which is exactly 1/2.

Now, substitute x = √3 in Option 3:

⇒ (x² − 1) / (1 + x²) = (3 − 1) / (1 + 3) = 2 / 4 = 1/2

∴ The correct answer is 1+x2x2−1​.

Alternate Method

Given:

secθ + tanθ = x --- (1)

Formula Used:

sec²θ − tan²θ = 1

Calculations:

⇒ (secθ + tanθ) × (secθ − tanθ) = 1

⇒ x × (secθ − tanθ) = 1

⇒ secθ − tanθ = 1/x --- (2)

Adding equation (1) and equation (2):

⇒ 2 × secθ = x + 1/x ⇒ secθ = (x² + 1) / 2x

Subtracting equation (2) from equation (1):

⇒ 2 × tanθ = x − 1/x ⇒ tanθ = (x² − 1) / 2x

From trigonometric ratios, we know secθ = Hypotenuse / Base and tanθ = Perpendicular / Base.

Comparing the values, we get Base = 2x, Perpendicular = x² − 1, and Hypotenuse = x² + 1.



⇒ sinθ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse

⇒ sinθ = (x² − 1) / (x² + 1)

∴ The correct answer is 1+x2x2−1​.

Additional Information

Pythagorean Triplets

In a right-angled triangle, hypotenuse² = perpendicular² + base². A highly useful variable triplet for trigonometry limits is (2x, x² − 1, x² + 1).

Trigonometric Identities

The three fundamental square identities are: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

Relation between Trigonometric Ratios

Basic conversions include tanθ = sinθ ÷ cosθ and secθ = 1 ÷ cosθ. Dividing these gives the direct relation sinθ = tanθ ÷ secθ.
